column1: To make our economy stronger and more productive, we must make health care more affordable, and give families greater access to good coverage. We've got to reform our welfare system, with strong work incentives, and clear expectations, so that more Americans can find good jobs and support their families. My administration is also committed to helping families buy homes, and creating an ownership society, where more Americans own a piece of the American dream. This is why I'm making it a priority to help families overcome the barriers to homeownership.

Americans can expect some things of me, as well. My most solemn responsibility is to protect the American people. I will never waver in defending our homeland and our interests. I will always put their safety first. I will ask Congress to provide our men and women in uniform with the resources they need to prevail in the war on terror. I will continue to work with our allies around the world to bring terrorists to justice, to deny them safe haven, and to prevent them from acquiring weapons of mass destruction.

When credible intelligence warrants, appropriate law enforcement and local officials are alerted. These warnings are, in turn, passed on to the public to help people prepare for potential emergencies. We are constantly working to improve our methods to keep our citizens safe. I take this responsibility very seriously, and I depend upon our talented, dedicated professionals to help me fulfill it. We remain vigilant amid these ever-present challenges to our nation's security, and always, always, our first consideration is the safety of the American people.

But the stakes for America are never small. If our country does not lead the world in confronting serious dangers, those dangers will not go away; they will gather and they will eventually reach our shores. Threats we face abroad are threats we will eventually face here. And so we must make sure we see it and we deal with it. We must make sure we have the capabilities to do so.

In all three aspects of our strategy -- security, democracy, and reconstruction -- we have made substantial progress. We're working with the Iraqi government to transfer sovereignty to the Iraqi people. We're building the capacity of Iraq's security forces, so they can defend their own country. And we're helping the Iraqi people rebuild their country. The progress, while real, has come hard. The enemy is fierce. They are testing our resolve, and they are testing the will of the Iraqi people.
